'''Puri''', also spelled '''poori''' is a fried [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]].

==Ingredients==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (60 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Whole Wheat|whole-wheat flour]]
* 2 oz (60 g) [[Cookbook:Flour#Wheat Flour|plain white flour]]
* 2 oz fine [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]] for the dough
* About 500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:Pint|pint]]) vegetable oil for [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Frying|deep frying]]
* [[Cookbook:Water|Water]] to mix the dough

==Procedure==

===Dough===
# Put all the dry ingredients into a bowl. 
# Add salt and drizzle the 1 tbsp oil over top. Mix well.
# Gradually mix in enough water to get a stiff [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the dough well for a few minutes.
# Cover the dough and leave to rest for about half an hour.

===Frying===
# Pour the oil for deep frying in a wok or other deep pan. Heat the oil.
# Meanwhile, divide the dough into 8 small balls and roll each into a small circle (about 3 [[Cookbook:Inch|in]] / 7.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] in diameter). You can use a bit of hot oil to roll the dough so it will not stick to the surface. 
# Check if the oil is hot enough—when you put a tiny piece of dough in the oil it should immediately rise to the surface. When the oil is ready, lay the flattened dough over the oil, press the top slightly with the slotted spoon until it inflates itself, and turn to other side. Adjust the flame as necessary.
# Remove the puri from the oil after it turns golden brown and place on a wire rack or kitchen paper towel for excess oil to drain.

==Notes, tips and variations==
* For chapatti dough, don't use semolina and plain flour. Only use whole wheat flour, salt, and oil.
* If the dough sinks quickly to the bottom of the wok, the oil is not hot enough and the puri will absorb too much oil. It should balloon within a few seconds.
